title: Camera
summary: The player's viewpoint: workspace.CurrentCamera. Controlled via CFrame, CameraType (Custom default; Scriptable for full control), FieldOfView, and CameraSubject for following.

properties.name: CFrame
properties.description: Camera position and orientation. Writing it moves the camera (fully effective when CameraType = Scriptable).

properties.name: CameraType
properties.description: Custom (default player camera), Scriptable (your code owns the CFrame), Follow, Track, Watch, Attach.

properties.name: CameraSubject
properties.description: What the default camera follows (usually the Humanoid).

properties.name: FieldOfView / FieldOfViewMode
properties.description: FOV in degrees (default 70) and interpretation axis.

properties.name: Focus
properties.description: Where the camera looks/renders with priority.

details.heading: Client domain
details.body: Each client owns its camera. Server writes to CurrentCamera don't do what you'd expect — camera work belongs in LocalScripts.

details.heading: Scriptable workflow
details.body: Set CameraType = Scriptable, drive CFrame each RenderStepped (or tween it), then restore CameraType = Custom to hand control back.

explanation.whatItIs: The window into your world. By default Roblox drives it (third-person orbit around the character); taking the wheel means Scriptable + CFrame math.
explanation.whyItExists: Everything the player sees flows through one camera — cutscenes, scopes, screenshakes, custom views all hook in here.
whenToUse: Screen shake: small random offsets each RenderStepped
whenNotToUse: From server Scripts — camera is per-client
Fighting the default camera every frame when a CameraType would do
explanation.mentalModel:
```text
Default: CameraType=Custom → Roblox orbits around CameraSubject
Cutscene: CameraType=Scriptable → you set CFrame every frame
End: back to Custom → player regains control
```
tips: Drive camera updates in RenderStepped for smoothness
Tween CFrame for cinematic moves; interpolate with CFrame:Lerp for follows
Always restore CameraType when your effect ends
commonMistakes: Writing camera CFrame without Scriptable — default camera fights back
Forgetting to restore FieldOfView/CameraType after effects

examples.title: Smooth cutscene pan
examples.code:
-- LocalScript
local camera = workspace.CurrentCamera
local startCF = camera.CFrame
local endCF = CFrame.new(0, 50, 0, 1, 0, 0, 0, -1, 0, 0, 0, -1)

camera.CameraType = Enum.CameraType.Scriptable

task.spawn(function()
    local DURATION = 3
    local t0 = os.clock()
    while true do
        local alpha = math.min(1, (os.clock() - t0) / DURATION)
        camera.CFrame = startCF:Lerp(endCF, alpha)
        if alpha >= 1 then break end
        task.wait()   -- yields to next frame
    end
    camera.CameraType = Enum.CameraType.Custom   -- hand it back
end)

examples.title: Simple screen shake
examples.code:
-- LocalScript, e.g. on explosion
local RunService = game:GetService("RunService")
local camera = workspace.CurrentCamera
local trauma = 1

local conn
conn = RunService.RenderStepped:Connect(function()
    trauma = math.max(0, trauma - 0.03)
    if trauma == 0 then conn:Disconnect() return end
    local shake = trauma * trauma * 1.5
    camera.CFrame *= CFrame.new(
        math.random(-100, 100) / 100 * shake,
        math.random(-100, 100) / 100 * shake,
        math.random(-100, 100) / 100 * shake
    )
end)
